chat.text:
> When is the live transcription actually sent to you, the smart assistant?

**How it works now**
- Both assistants hear the same lines. The fast assistant doesn't hand anything to me. It only answers quickly, then stays quiet.
- I'm not woken per sentence. Your lines are batched and reach me when you pause, ask something, speak to me by name, or six sentences pile up. The last line of each batch says which: `(paused 6 s)`, `(asked)`, `(6 sentences)`, or `(the mic went off)`.
- That batching is the delay you felt. Typed lines arrive after a short moment.
- Lines dictated before your refresh most likely stayed in the page's buffer and were never posted to the session. I can't confirm that from here.

**Showing it in the UI**
- I don't know of a marker in the dictate UI today that shows when a line goes to me. This is a dictation change, so `mastermind-dictation-2` owns it.
- I asked you a question on your prompt: do you want a "sent to smart assistant" marker on each dictated line? Say yes and I'll pass it to that mastermind.

sections.heading: ↩️ Moving a chat card for reference

items.text: No need to design this first since it's not what's being worked on right now — just noting it in case it didn't make it into the system yet.

**Prompt class:** it lives in `core/Task/Prompt.js`. Every card in your session file is written as a `Prompt`, but Chat v2 doesn't use that class and keeps its own copy.

**What I did**
- I filed a task for context cards and the Question class.
- I sent your points to `mastermind-dictation-2`: topic cards holding questions and tasks, one refinement driving both V1 and V2, and a Question that extends Task and stays open until you accept the answer.
- A cheap agent is checking past work on the Question class and on how prompts, replies, questions and tasks are logged. I'll relay what it finds.

chat.text: Why would chat to not use that class and keep its own copy?

I don't know the reason, and I haven't seen the history. My guess is that Chat v2 was built quickly in a separate pass without wiring in the shared class. The plan already fixes this: step 3 puts V1 and V2 on one reader built from the real `Prompt` class. The copy is what caused the checkbox bug.

The Question class already exists, so nobody needs to build it.

```
core/Task/Question.js   extends Task
  open -> answered -> complete   (complete = owner has read the answer)
core/Task/Prompt.js     extends Task
  raw[], paragraphs[{id,text}], sentences (computed: a1, a2...),
  replies[{id,text,by,anchor}], refined, notes, parts
session.jsonl           one list of tasks; replies and answers live ON
                        what they answer (prompt.replies, question.answer)
```

- **Question completion:** an answered question completes when the owner reads the answer, which matches your rule.
- **Log shape:** the session holds one list of items, and replies and answers sit on what they answer. That is your 2026-10-25 decision, documented in `dictation-debug/chat-shape.md`.

So the remaining work is getting V1 and V2 to use these classes, and drawing question widgets and cards.

⬜ How the prompt renders as chat bubbles and groups needs a solid look — it's probably different between V1 and V2, and the two need to be unified

When a question is asked it should be upgraded into its own question card — a little question icon block, created the same way a task is — and the answer gets added to it when it comes in; questions need to be referenceable

A question is created inside the context block currently being worked in — a context block is like a chat bubble you can put things into, made for whatever's being discussed, and titled as part of the refinement process
Whatever topic is being talked about shows on screen, a new topic appears when you switch, and a question goes to the root if it doesn't belong to a topic or into that topic's block if it does

This isn't critical for dictation specifically right now, but getting these conversation cards working matters — adapting live to what's said, merging each clean sentence into its card (e.g. a question sentence gets associated with the question card)
A Question class should extend Task — though check whether that's right for the dictation mastermind first, since this was already discussed yesterday
Question can extend Task because both share the same completion idea: a question isn't complete until it's answered
A question should stay incomplete until its answer is accepted, not just given — asking means not understanding yet, and unanswered questions need to keep resurfacing until satisfied
⬜ Launch a secondary agent to build the Question class, but generalize it so any kind of card — question, statement, task, etc. — can be created the same way

p-1792965434620.title: Routing for clickable cards in the global sheet
p-1792965434620.text: Chat should be the same code as the session detail page. Cards click through to a detail view (preview card -> full render, swapping the chat area, with a way back). Reload must keep the spot. The global sheet cannot own the URL path (site navigation must keep working). Options: no routing (UI-only state), a query-string variable, or the existing router on a session's own page. No new elaborate routing system.

add.title: Spawn fresh child agents; stop reviving old sessions
add.description: Reviving an old session (mastermind-dictation-2, parented to vscode-mastermind) credits its cost and task completion to the old parent. Write the rule in system docs: start fresh sub-sessions of this session, revive only in rare cases; masterminds must document state so a fresh one can resume. Audit that every task asked for in this chat is attributed to this session and completed.

p-1792965565590.title: Fresh sessions, not revived ones (accounting)
p-1792965565590.text: Reviving old agents misattributes cost and task completion to the original parent. Document: spawn fresh child sessions; masterminds keep state documented. Audit that all tasks asked in this chat are counted under this session and get completed.

p-1792966091101.title: Converge outcomes; fast=place, smart=title/restructure
p-1792966091101.text: V1 compact, V2 cards rich but lists not rendered as lists. One data structure for both. Fast assistant: place each sentence (and turn questions into Question items) and stop; smart assistant: titles and restructuring, reliably. Show live raw whisper in V2. > Does the smart assistant tail the fast assistant's work?

No. I'm woken by batches of your raw lines (a 12 s pause, a question, my name, or 6 sentences), not by each sentence the fast assistant places. Waking me on each placed sentence is possible, and you said the token cost is fine. I've asked `mastermind-dictation-2` what wires that and what it would take.

The rest went to `mastermind-dictation-2` as asks and is logged on your prompt:
- **Roles:** the fast assistant places each sentence and turns questions into Question items. I write titles and restructure.
- **Live text:** V2 shows the live raw whisper text.
- **Cards:** refined cards converge into ranked outcomes and open decisions instead of growing.
- **Lists:** numbered lists render as real lists.
- **Timeout:** it checks whether the send-after-pause timeout should come down.

> Do we use the Session class server side, and can a session tail its own log?

From a quick code check, which I haven't double-checked:

- **Session class:** yes, Servex uses the framework's Session class (`core/Session/Session.js:18`). `Servex/agents/Agents.js:65` registers resolvers on it, so it runs server side too and isn't only a browser view.
- **Tailing:** the existing follow tool (`Servex/Follow.js`) already accepts voice sessions. Follow delivers new lines of a `session.jsonl` into an agent's inbox, and the agent reads them with `updates()` (`Servex/agents/External.js:120-135`). The file watch is on the server, not the browser dev socket.
- **Consequence:** I can tail my own `session.jsonl` today with `follow` and `updates()`. That means no new transport, which fits what you asked for. The change is to swap my wake rules (12 s pause, question, name, 6 sentences) for follow.

No, it isn't limited to one task, and nothing in the code enforces that. The name only says what it was started for. In `roles.js` it's just a `mastermind` with no path, so it can work on whatever you give it. That's why the name is confusing: it suggests a task link that doesn't exist.

A mastermind named for its job and its folder is clearer, such as `mastermind-chat` at `public/framework/ux/Dictate`. The docs fix already asked for covers that, and the two running ones keep their current names until they finish.

> What is a prompt, and are V1 bubbles and V2 cards the same thing?

A prompt is one thought of yours: the raw words plus a cleaned version, with its replies, questions and tasks attached. Both V1 and V2 draw it as one visual unit, a bubble in V1 and a card in V2. The difference is what they read. V1 reads chat lines. V2 reads the prompt record itself, with its sentences, replies and tasks. Unifying the two on the prompt record is the open reader task with `task-mastermind-2`, so that one prompt shows the same everywhere.

> How could the smart assistant work dynamically, autonomously and quickly, if it blocks on long reads?

My recommendation is to keep the smart seat thin and never let it dig itself:
- **Smart seat:** it answers, routes and files tasks. It stays free to take the next sentence.

- **RAM:** short-lived workers hold memory for seconds, not minutes, so the 2.5 GB limit is less of a problem. Long-running masterminds remain for real build work.

> How does it work: socket or not, dev server or Servex?

It goes to Servex, over plain HTTP in both directions. There's no socket. The doc has these stages:

1. **Whisper:** the page sends audio to the `whisper-server` and re-sends the growing sentence every 0.9 s (`Dictate.js:575`, `Mic.js:20`).
2. **Live bubble:** the draft shows on the page only (`Chat.js:794`). Nothing is saved yet.
3. **Send:** on a pause, the page posts the text to Servex at `/api/session/say` (`chat.js:178`).
4. **Save:** `Sessions.js:930` writes the line into `session.jsonl` and opens or grows the prompt. Servex is the only writer.
5. **Fast assistant:** the line waits 2.5 s of quiet, then goes to the fast seat, which writes a placement line per sentence (`Sessions.js:970`, `:438`).
6. **Smart assistant:** it is woken in batches (`Sessions.js:255`) and writes titles, replies, tasks and questions with the item tool.
7. **Back to the screen:** new lines come back over a streaming connection, `GET /api/session/<id>/stream` (an EventSource), plus a file poll every 1.5 s as backup.

> What triggers what for the cursors?

Each cursor moves when its line is written to `session.jsonl`, never earlier:
- **Gray ✓:** your sentence is saved and sent to fast.
- **Green ✓:** fast writes its placement line for that sentence, so fast has finished its work first.
- **Gray 🧠:** the sentence is delivered to smart (`feed_smart`).
- **Pink 🧠:** smart's first write for it lands, such as the working sign, a title or a reply. It does its work first, then the cursor changes.

So the screen only changes when the file does, and nothing is faked ahead of the work. The last review noted that the 🧠 colors in the current build are reversed. That is being fixed in round 4.

> Can the POST for a chunk get a long-lived delayed response?

Technically yes. The server can hold a request open for 10 to 30 s and answer when the agent is done. I'd advise against it:
- **Browser limit:** a browser allows only about 6 open connections per host. With a request per sentence, a few slow answers would block the next sends.
- **Fragility:** an open request dies on a page reload or a Servex restart, so you'd lose the result.
- **Already covered:** the streaming connection already carries results back. The planned per-chunk done line gives the same signal without holding anything open.

So the POST stays "got it", the done line is the real answer, and the stream delivers it.

> What did we figure out on the Whisper chunking and mangling?

**How Whisper is chunked**
- **Requests:** an interim request about every 0.9 s with all audio since the last pause, then one final request at a 0.7 s pause or the 15 s cap.
- **Memory:** each request is independent, and our client sends no prompt to Whisper.
- **Seams:** nothing stitches segments together.

**Mangling**
- **Duplicates:** `Mic.js` sends Whisper's live guess early. When the final rewords it, the matching fails and the already-sent words go out again. That is the overlapping lines.
- **Timing:** it started before today's merges. The rate was 14% of lines at 17:00 and 24% at 18:00.
- **Chopped fronts:** the mid-word chops ("ogged.") are unexplained so far. We need Whisper's raw output to tell whether the audio or the text code is at fault.

**In flight**
- `minion-dictation-mangle` is fixing the duplicates with a replay test, and logging Whisper's raw output.
- `minion-wake-count` is making smart count only finished sentences.

Here's what "since the last pause" means. The page keeps recording while you talk. Each time you stop for 0.7 s, it closes that stretch and starts fresh. Every 0.9 s while you speak, it sends Whisper the whole stretch so far, not just the newest bit.

2. About 0.9 s in, it sends Whisper everything recorded so far, 0.9 s of audio. The gray guess appears.

4. This repeats every 0.9 s, with the audio growing each time.
5. You stop for 0.7 s. The page sends the whole stretch once more as the final, and it turns black.
6. The next thing you say starts a fresh stretch at zero.

Each request is bigger than the last, and Whisper redoes the whole stretch each time. The reason is that Whisper does better with the whole sentence than with small pieces. The cost is that the text keeps changing until the final. I'm going from the code summary, not running a timer, so the exact numbers could be a little off.

It's 15. I searched the code and there is no 9 s value anywhere. The "9 seconds" in your lines is a mangled echo of your own speech.

The full set of pause timings is:
- **0.7 s of silence:** closes the segment and sends the final to Whisper.
- **15 s of talking:** forces a cut, even with no pause.
- **0.9 s:** how often the growing segment is re-sent as a gray guess. Whisper answers in about 70 ms.
- **2.5 s of silence:** the mic stops, in send-on-pause mode. This is the same 2.5 s as the server's hold, after which the fast assistant gets the line.
- **12 s of quiet:** the old smart wake rule. With sentences set to 1, it rarely matters.

> Give me an example of how the data flows from the POST to the stream. Which line does Servex hand over?

"The line" means one chunk of your speech. For example, you say "Make the gap smaller."

1. **Page to Servex.** Your browser sends `POST /api/session/say` with that text. Servex answers "ok" straight away, and that request is finished.
2. **Servex writes it.** Servex appends two lines to `session.jsonl`: your words as a `chat` line, and a Prompt line (`raw: "Make the gap smaller."`). Servex is the only writer.
3. **Servex hands it to the assistants.** This is the "line" I meant. It's the same text, passed in memory to the fast assistant, and later to the smart one. It isn't a file or a network call.
4. **The assistants write back.** The fast assistant produces a `place` line. The smart one writes a reply with the item tool. Each goes through Servex into `session.jsonl`.
5. **The stream pushes it to the page.** Your browser opened one long connection to `GET /api/session/<id>/stream` when the session started. Every new line in the file is pushed down that connection as it is written, so the page draws it without asking.
6. **The backup.** The page also re-reads the file every 1.5 s. If the stream drops, the same lines still arrive.

So the POST only goes up and the stream only comes down. The ✓ and 🧠 cursors are lines coming down the stream. The proposed chunk id is a tag in step 1 that the lines in step 4 carry back, so the page can match each answer to its chunk.

> How are sentences stored in the prompt system? Does each get an id? Are we using prompt instances?

**Stored.** Each Prompt (`core/Task/Prompt.js:35`) holds:
- `raw`: a list of the chunks as Whisper gave them. One entry is pushed per chunk.
- `paragraphs`: a list like `{id: "a", text: "…"}`. Each new chunk is appended to the open paragraph. The id is a letter.
- `title`, `text` (my cleaned version), `replies`, `tasks`. I write these.

**Not stored.** Sentences are computed from a paragraph's text each time (`Prompt.split` at :53, `ChatV2Model.sentences` at :84). A sentence's id is the paragraph id plus its number: `a1`, `a2`, `b1`. Nothing writes sentence by sentence into the file.

**Instances.** The classes exist (Prompt, Paragraph, Question, Reply) in core, but Chat v2 doesn't use them. It folds the log lines by hand in `ChatV2Model.js`, a decision recorded in the Chat v2 readme.

**Why it matters.** Replies and questions point at a sentence by `a2`. That works only while the paragraph text doesn't change, because the number is its position. A stored per-sentence structure with permanent ids is the sentence-by-sentence breakdown we discussed, and it isn't built. It would fit the chunk-id work: one id per sentence, assigned at write time.

> Is the fast assistant a fresh request per chunk? Do we create a new session id for every chunk?

No. The fast assistant is one long-lived agent per voice session, `voice-assistant-v-sq8y7db`. It appears in the process list as a single running process. Servex prewarms it when the session is created (`Sessions.js:792`) and feeds it each chunk as another message to the same agent, through `voice_say`. So there's one session id for the whole conversation, and it remembers the earlier chunks. That's how it can place a new chunk into the old prompt or a new one.

**Cost.** Its context grows with every chunk and is compacted when full. This is a likely reason the session gets heavy over a long dictation.

I haven't read how the compaction or any reset works for the fast seat. The architect's doc, `fast-and-smart.md`, lists models and prompts per seat. I can ask it to add the context handling if you want.

> Could the ids and the report-back work automatically, with no AI needing to remember anything?

Yes. Servex can do all of it in code.

- **Ids:** the page stamps each chunk with an id before sending. The AI never sees or makes one.
- **Placed (✓):** when the fast assistant's turn on that chunk ends, Servex writes the "placed" line itself. That's the turn finishing, not the AI saying anything.
- **Handled (🧠):** the same for the smart assistant. Servex writes the "handled" line when the turn it started for those sentences ends.
- **Raw words:** the server keeps each chunk's raw text under its id. The AI only adds its cleaned version.

So an AI that forgets, or does nothing, still gets its chunk marked as handled, because the mark follows the turn ending and not the AI's own words. The one caveat: "handled" then means "the assistant finished its turn", not "it made a task". I think that's right for a cursor.

Today the data looks like this:

```
Prompt p-1792979067311          (id = time in ms)
  raw: "…"                      (what Whisper heard)
  paragraphs: a: "…", b: "…"    (lettered ids)
  sentences: a1, a2, b1         (computed, not stored)
  title, text                   (smart's refined version)
  replies / tasks / questions   (children, each with an id)
```

The new id isn't a new kind. The page already stamps every spoken line with a time, and Prompts already use time-in-ms ids (`p-<ms>`).

My proposal is to make a chunk's id that same stamp, `c-<ms>`, on the raw line the page sends:

```
raw line:  {c: "c-1792979067311", text: "…"}
placed:    {placed: "c-1792979067311", by: fast}
handled:   {handled: "c-1792979067311", by: smart}
```

So the cursor matches by id. The chunk belongs to a Prompt, and a sentence is just a chunk with an outcome (task, question or note).

The open question is whether chunk ids and the computed sentence ids (`a1`, `a2`) should be the same thing. I think the data structure task should decide that before anything is built, and the design should settle it first.

In plain terms, a chunk id is a name tag on each piece of speech, and a placed/handled report is a "done" slip tied to that tag.

**Why it avoids races**
- **Append-only log:** only Servex writes, one line at a time, so two writers can't clash. This is already how the session works.
- **Match by id, not by order:** replies can arrive late or out of order, and the cursor still finds the right chunk by its tag. Today's guessing by order is what makes the cursors inaccurate.
- **Done slip is written by code:** when an assistant's turn ends, Servex writes the slip. No AI has to remember, and a slow or silent AI can't leave a cursor stuck, because the turn ending is the trigger.
- **Safe to repeat:** a duplicate slip does nothing, and a missing one leaves the cursor gray.

**Where trouble could still come from**
- Two chunks sent in quick succession, and one assistant's turn covering both. Handle it by having the slip list all the ids that turn covered.
- A restart in the middle. The log survives it, and the next start can replay it.

I'm fairly confident in the approach, and it's the standard shape for this problem. The part I'd still check is how the id relates to sentence ids, and that's why the data structure design comes first.

You say: "Can you hear me? I was in another tab."

**1. The page cuts it into chunks and stamps each with an id**
```
c-100  "Can you hear me?"
c-200  "I was in another tab."
```

**2. Each chunk is sent to the server as one line**
```
{ say: "c-100", text: "Can you hear me?" }
{ say: "c-200", text: "I was in another tab." }
```

**3. The page draws cursors on those two chunks**
```
Can you hear me?        ✓gray 🧠gray
I was in another tab.   ✓gray 🧠gray
```

**4. Servex writes a "done" line when each assistant finishes**
```
{ placed:  "c-100", by: "fast"  }     -> ✓ turns green on c-100
{ placed:  "c-200", by: "fast"  }     -> ✓ turns green on c-200
{ handled: ["c-100","c-200"], by: "smart" }  -> 🧠 turns pink on both
```

**5. What the smart assistant produces points back at the chunks**
```
Question q-1  from: "c-100"   "Can you hear me?"   answer: "Yes."
Note     n-1  from: "c-200"   "was in another tab"
```

That's all a chunk id is: a name on the piece of speech that the cursors, the done lines and the question or task cards all point back to. Is that clearer?

> What problem does this solve?

**The problem:** you want to see, as you talk, that each thing you said was heard and acted on. Today the UI can't know that. It only knows it sent something, so the cursors turn green or pink too early, and the cleaned lines can land in the wrong place.

**The solution:** each piece of speech gets a name tag. When the fast or smart assistant finishes with it, the server tells the UI "that one is done". The cursors then show what really happened.

**Why it matters:** you can trust the cursors, and you don't need to reread the chat to check that something wasn't dropped.

You're right that it's the fast and smart assistants notifying the UI. The id is only how the UI knows which piece they mean.

Here is the shape as a tree, with what each part is:

```
Session
├─ chat lines      what you said, one per chunk (the raw record)
└─ tasks (a list of items)
   ├─ Prompt       one thought of yours
   │   ├─ raw         your exact words
   │   ├─ paragraphs  the cleaned text, grouped

   │        ├─ Question   (with its answer)
   │        ├─ Task
   │        └─ replies
   └─ other tasks  (not from a Prompt)
```

- **chat** is the stream of what was said.
- **tasks** is the list of things made from it.
- A **Prompt** is the link between them: it names the chunks it came from and holds the outcomes.

**The data flow**
- **Session item:** has no `chat` List. A `{chat:{…}}` line is stored as one plain property, so the newest chat object overwrites the last one. It never keeps the chat.
- **V1:** doesn't use the item at all. It reads the raw `chat` lines from the stream and builds its bubbles in the browser.
- **V2:** reads the Prompts, Questions and Tasks in the `tasks` list. The chat lines are only the raw record behind them.

So there are two readers and two shapes.

**Fix**
- Add a `chat` List on the Session, with items keyed by `at`. That is a small change.
- The real work is moving V1's Widget onto it.
- With that List, both views draw from one place. It belongs in the data-structure design.

dictate-one-solid-data-structure-for-pro.description: Design a rock-solid data structure for prompts, their sentences, the refining, and attribution: every sentence is attributed to a specific outcome, which is a task, a question, or a note. A note is the outcome type with no real outcome: just a message or note. Owner (2026-10-25): V1 and V2 must NOT have two data flows. Unify the data structure and the API (what the page reads and what the seats write); the UI (bubbles, CSS) matters less and each of V1 and V2 can configure how it shows the same data. Today V1 reads raw `chat` lines via ext/Session/Session.js entry() and ux/Dictate/Widget.js; V2 reads the Prompts/Questions/Tasks in `tasks` via ChatV2Model.js; the Session item has no chat List (core/Session/Session.js:91-127 stores a chat line as one overwritten property). Candidate: a `chat` List on the Session keyed by `at`, with both views drawing Prompts. Chunk ids/acks (existing `at` as the id) and fewer log lines per thought belong to this design. Do the design first, before more changes to the chat.

The line holds my text and `re`, the time of your line it answers. Servex writes it when my turn ends, so I don't write it myself. Each of my chat replies is one `chat` line, and each also makes a `sent` line (`{"sent":{"to":"smart","re":[...]}}`) that records my turn picking up your words. Short replies are cheap, but the two lines per reply add up over a long session. That's one more reason for the one-conclusive-line design.

You're right, and it's a flaw, not a design. The `chat` line looks like a property in the file but the Session doesn't implement it, so replay just overwrites a single value. Either `chat` becomes a real List, or chat lines stop looking like properties. Making it a List (keyed by `at`) is my recommendation, and it's in the design doc.

```
session.jsonl   (file on disk, one JSON object per line)
   |  Servex reads it, then watches for new lines
   v
/api/session/<id>/stream   (the live feed)
   |  sends every old line first, then each new one
   v
the page (browser)
   |  Session.apply_line(line)  -> real children: tasks, Prompts...
   |  entry(line)               -> V1: chat lines become bubbles
   v
what is drawn: V2 draws the Prompts in `tasks`; V1 draws the entries from entry()
```

The only gap is the `chat` step. For `tasks`, the page's Session item holds the records. For `chat`, V1 builds its own list in a separate step.

V1 doesn't use the EventSource. `Session.watch` in `ext/Session/Session.js` polls the file itself over plain HTTP: it fetches `session.jsonl`, asking only for the bytes after where it last stopped (a `Range` request), and splits them into lines. On the first read it hands the page the whole history. After that it checks every second or so for new lines.

So on reload V1 downloads the whole file again, and each line goes through `entry()` to become a prompt, a reply, or an invisible update. The EventSource feed exists too (it's what Servex uses), but this V1 code path doesn't depend on it.

The bubbles are therefore drawn from the file itself, and the Session's `chat` property isn't involved. That part of what I said was right, but I should have described the poll, not the EventSource.

Right now, in V1:

1. `Session.watch` fetches `session.jsonl` over HTTP and reads it from the start, then keeps asking for newer bytes about every second.
2. Each line goes to `entry()`, which turns `chat` lines into prompts (yours) and replies (assistants), and drops the invisible kinds.
3. `Widget.js` collects those entries in a `Thread`, merges your lines within 8 s into one bubble, and draws them.

The Session item and its `tasks` list play no part in it.

The build so far only saves bytes, not the cursor signal.

- **Raw words:** stored once per thought, at close.

**Not built yet:** the placed/handled signal, fewer lines per thought, and the Mic.js fixes. The next minion does these.

Owner's model (2026-10-25): NO separate chat list. The session has ONE list (its `tasks`): Prompts, Questions, Tasks, notes. Each Prompt is the first contextual block; every assistant response is added to a specific Prompt block, never to a free chat list. The fast and smart seats chunk the speech into logical blocks and put each response in the right place. That one list is the primary view for BOTH V1 and V2: unify the data structure and the API, the UI (bubbles, CSS) matters less and each view may configure how it shows the same data. V1 is very chat-based today, so moving it is the tricky part. Today: V1 reads raw `chat` lines via ext/Session/Session.js watch()+entry() (ux/Dictate/chat.js:293); V2 reads Prompts in `tasks` via ChatV2Model.js; core/Session/Session.js:125 stores a `chat` line as one overwritten property (dead). Chunk ids/acks (existing `at` as the id), fewer log lines per thought, and raw stored once belong to this design. Do the design first, before more changes to the chat.

Related: replies splitting a bubble mid-dictation; hold replies while dictating.

> Chunking of the prompts

**Three steps, each cutting the stream differently:**
- **Audio to lines.** Whisper turns your speech into short text chunks. Each becomes one chat line, and its `at` time is its id.
- **Lines to Prompts.** The fast seat sees every chunk. It places each one in the same paragraph, a new paragraph, or a new Prompt. A Prompt closes after a quiet gap (`prompt_close_ms`).
- **Prompts to the smart seat.** I get a batch when a sentence ends (`.?!`), you pause, or six sentences pile up.

**The bug:** a reply also closes the Prompt (`prompt_close_on_reply`). That splits your bubble mid-dictation. The fix is to hold replies until you pause for about a second.

Your fear is correct. Session replay knows only a few verbs.

**Real, handled by `apply_line` (`core/Session/Session.js:91-127`)**
- `tasks`, plus the `task`/`as` reference line.
- `stop` and `start`.
- `settings`, which is merged.
- `decide`.
- A card id (`{"<id>":{…}}`), which goes to that nested item.

**Everything else falls through to `this.put(k, v)` (:125)**
- `chat`, `place`, `sent`, `react`, `quiet`, `pause`, `nav`, `refined`, `log` and `find` are each stored as a single property, and the latest value overwrites the one before. `ts` and `by` are stamps.
- Nothing models them as items, so no history is kept in the replayed state. The readers that need history re-scan the file themselves, which is why V1 polls and redraws.

**Who reads them**
- V1 draws from `chat`.
- V2 reads `chat` and `sent` (`ChatV2Model.js:18,20`).
- `place` appears to be read mainly by the V1 and dictation code. The doc is confirming that.

So any new signal built as a loose key like `placed` or `handled` would be another magic word. That is why I paused chunk-ack-2. The doc's keys table will give the final per-key answer.

**Mostly no, with one exception.** I read the code (`ext/Session/Session.js:223-263`, `ux/Dictate/chat.js:215-293`).

**Not reprocessed on every poll.** After the first read, each poll fetches only the new bytes (a `Range` request from the stored offset). Each line is parsed once and handed on. So the "second fetch" fear is wrong.

**But there are separate readers.** Each new line in V1 goes through `draw`, which feeds two different interpretations:
- The `entry()` path turns `chat`/`refined`/`para` lines into bubbles (`Session.js:266-292`).
- `ChatV2Model` folds the same line a second time for Tasks and Questions (`chat.js:215-218`).

Neither uses the canonical `Session.apply_line`, which Servex and the session pages use. So there are three interpreters of one file, and each plucks out what it understands. That is the thing to unify.

**The exception:** a page load reads the whole 2.4 MB file and parses every line.

## Ids, from the code

- **Who mints:** `Item` mints ids as random UUIDs (`Item.js:35,274`), and only when the caller leaves the id out. The List does not mint. Prompt, question and reply ids (`p-`, `q-`, `r-`) are made by hand today (`PromptLines.js:26-28`).
- **Risk:** an add line with no id replays to a new random UUID each time, so a delta by id would miss it. Whether the item tool writes the minted id back into the line is not verified.
- **Replies:** a Prompt already has a real `replies` List (`core/Task/Prompt.js:74`), but its items are untyped, V1 never reads it, and Questions and Tasks sit in a separate list.
- **Recommendation:** the List mints `<ms>[-n]` on add and writes it into the line. That is immutable, sortable and readable, with no UUID. The target is one typed `content` list per Prompt.

## What the doc found

**Why V1 is jumpy**
- **Reset bug:** `Widget.reset()` never clears `task_rows`, so Question and Task rows don't come back after a reattach (`Widget.js:692-701`). It's a one-line fix.
- **Double delivery:** the poll and the live stream both call `draw`, and only `chat` and `refined` lines are deduped. Task rows are torn down and rebuilt a moment after they first appear, which looks like a flash. Adding the same dedup to the other kinds removes most of it.
- **Two channels with different timing:** there is no small fix for this one, but the dedup reduces most of the churn.

**The "S1, open" note**
- Refine runs on each single chat line, not on the whole Prompt (`Sessions.js:994`).
- Short lines fail the `worth_refining` gate and never get refined at all.
- The fix is to refine the Prompt's accumulated text instead, and anchor the result to the Prompt's id.

One catch: if no item matches that id, the key isn't deleted. It falls through to `this.put(k, v)` (`Session.js:125`), and the session ends up with a stray property named after the id. ## The flow, from voice to Prompt

1. **Browser mic.** Whisper transcribes your speech. The browser sends a chunk at every `.` `!` `?` (commas are off). If you go quiet for 2 s, it sends whatever is left (`Mic.js`).
2. **Servex writes a `chat` line** for each chunk, with `at` as its id. It also opens the Prompt in the `tasks` list, or adds to the open one: your raw words, plus paragraph "a" growing in place.
3. **Fast seat** (Haiku) gets the chunk. It writes a `{place}` line saying same paragraph, new paragraph, or card. A "?" sentence also gets a Question.
4. **Smart seat** (me) gets a batch when a sentence ends (`.?!`), you pause, or six sentences pile up. I refine the title and text, answer, and file tasks.
5. **The Prompt closes** after a quiet gap, and the next chunk starts a new one.

**Sentences** aren't stored. They're computed from the paragraph text (`a1`, `a2`). So a chunk is a sentence or a phrase ending in punctuation, and a Prompt is a run of chunks with no long pause between them.
